children: Phoenix Education Partners agreed to acquire Fuel50, an artificial-intelligence workforce-transformation platform.
The parent company of the University of Phoenix said Fuel50 would advance its strategy of providing skills-focused education to working adults and employers.
Fuel50 is expected to remain a distinct business after the deal, with co-founder and President Jo Mills expected to assume the role of Fuel50's chief executive officer.
Financial terms of the deal weren't disclosed. The deal is expected to close within 30 days.

"Fuel50 has built an impressive platform, deep workforce expertise and a compelling vision for helping employers understand changing skill needs and develop and mobilize talent," Phoenix Education Partners CEO Chris Lynne said. "We believe strongly in Fuel50's future and are excited to support its continued innovation and to help extend its impact with employers navigating workforce transformation."
